guide.headline: Bills run the Patriots front into the ground
guide.hook: Buffalo's ground game and Josh Allen's efficient arm meet a Patriots defense that can't stop the run, and this one could get out of hand early.

items.title: Bills ground game owns the line
items.what: The Bills rank No. 3 of 32 in rush EPA per carry at 0.08, and the Patriots rank No. 27 against the run by that same measure at 0.03. That's a 78 percentile point gap, not a lean. If Buffalo's backs are hitting the second level untouched in the first quarter, the line of scrimmage belongs to them all afternoon.
items.when: Watch the first ten Bills carries of the game.
items.who: Bills ground game vs Patriots run front

items.title: Allen stays efficient outside the numbers
items.what: Josh Allen is completing passes at a CPOE of plus 4.5 with a 9.1 yards per attempt average, good for the top 11 percent of NFL quarterbacks this season. He's thrown 5 touchdowns to 2 interceptions on 786 yards, and his game is about ball placement outside the numbers and resetting his feet when the first read is covered.
items.when: Watch him on first and second down throws outside the hashes.

items.title: Bills convert the long downs
items.what: Buffalo ranks No. 5 of 32 on passing downs at a 49 percent success rate, while New England ranks just No. 12 defending those downs at 35 percent. That's a 22 percentile point edge, meaning a third-and-8 is not an automatic stop for the Patriots. Two conversions like that in the first half can break the defensive plan entirely.
items.when: Watch the Bills on third-and-long in the first half.
items.who: Bills on passing downs vs Patriots pressure

guide.cardLine: Buffalo's No. 3 rush offense meets New England's No. 27 run defense, a 78 percentile point gap that could decide this early.
